item_description: A major Egyptian deity whose worship became closely associated with the sun god Ra as Amun-Ra.
item_facts: Amun was especially important at Thebes.
His name is commonly interpreted as 'the hidden one,' though translations vary.
His attributes changed across periods and local traditions.
needs_review: Verify transliteration and historical development using Egyptological references.

item_description: An ancient Egyptian deity associated with embalming, funerary rites and the protection of the dead.
item_facts: Anubis is commonly depicted with a jackal head.
He appears in funerary texts and scenes involving judgment of the dead.
His prominence shifted as Osiris became more central to afterlife beliefs.
needs_review: Verify period-specific roles and iconography through museum or Egyptological sources.

item_description: An Egyptian goddess associated with protection, fertility and domestic life, often represented as a cat or lioness.
item_facts: Bastet was worshipped prominently at Bubastis.
Her imagery shifted over time from lioness to domestic cat associations.
She could be connected with protection and childbirth.
needs_review: Verify changes in iconography and roles by historical period.

item_description: The Egyptian god associated with the earth and a member of the Heliopolitan creation tradition.
item_facts: Geb is paired with the sky goddess Nut in Egyptian cosmology.
Their children include Osiris, Isis, Seth and Nephthys in a major tradition.
He is sometimes depicted with vegetation or a goose symbol.
needs_review: Verify myth versions and iconographic details with Egyptological sources.

item_description: A widely worshipped Egyptian goddess associated with music, joy, love and motherhood.
item_facts: Hathor was often represented with cow imagery or a sun disk between horns.
She was associated with the sky and with protection of the king.
Her worship had important centers including Dendera.
needs_review: Verify iconography and cult history across periods using Egyptological references.

item_description: A falcon-associated Egyptian deity linked with kingship and the protection of the ruler.
item_facts: The living pharaoh was often associated with Horus.
Horus’s conflict with Seth appears in several myth traditions.
Horus and other deities were merged or identified in different historical contexts.
needs_review: Distinguish forms of Horus and myth variants using scholarly sources.

item_description: A major Egyptian goddess associated with magic, healing, motherhood and the protection of Osiris and Horus.
item_facts: Isis is central to the Osiris myth cycle.
Her worship spread beyond Egypt in the Greco-Roman world.
She was often depicted with a throne-shaped hieroglyph or later with cow horns and a sun disk.
needs_review: Verify iconographic development and regional worship history.

item_description: A scarab-associated Egyptian deity linked with the rising sun and renewal.
item_facts: Khepri is associated with the sun’s emergence at dawn.
The scarab beetle served as a symbol of transformation and renewal.
Khepri could be understood as one aspect of the sun god across the day.
needs_review: Verify theological interpretation and spellings with Egyptological sources.

item_description: A moon deity worshipped at Thebes and part of the Theban triad with Amun and Mut.
item_facts: Khonsu is associated with the moon and the passage of time.
He was worshipped at the Karnak temple complex.
Some traditions associate him with healing.
needs_review: Verify local cult roles and myth references using Egyptological sources.

item_description: The Egyptian concept and personification of truth, justice, balance and cosmic order.
item_facts: Ma’at was represented as a goddess wearing an ostrich feather.
The feather of Ma’at appears in depictions of the weighing of the heart.
The concept informed Egyptian ideas of ethical and political order.
needs_review: Verify textual nuance and avoid reducing a complex concept to a single translation.

item_description: An Egyptian goddess associated with mourning and protection, especially in funerary contexts.
item_facts: Nephthys is a sister of Isis and Osiris in a major myth tradition.
She assists Isis in mourning and protecting the dead.
Her name is written with a hieroglyph associated with a temple enclosure.
needs_review: Verify relationships, roles and name interpretation in Egyptological sources.

item_description: The Egyptian sky goddess, often depicted arching over the earth god Geb.
item_facts: Nut and Geb are separated in Egyptian creation imagery.
She is the mother of Osiris, Isis, Seth and Nephthys in a common tradition.
Funerary texts associate Nut with the protection and rebirth of the dead.
needs_review: Verify myth versions and funerary roles from Egyptological references.

item_description: An Egyptian god associated with the dead, resurrection and the afterlife, and ruler of the underworld in many traditions.
item_facts: The Osiris myth tells of his death and restoration by Isis.
Osiris was connected with agricultural renewal and kingship.
Deceased people could be identified with Osiris in funerary beliefs.
needs_review: Verify interpretive nuance and regional variation in the Osiris tradition.

item_description: A creator deity and patron of craftsmen whose major cult center was Memphis.
item_facts: Ptah was especially worshipped at Memphis.
A theological text describes creation through the heart and tongue.
He was associated with artisans and builders.
needs_review: Verify the source and interpretation of the Memphis theology text.

item_description: A major Egyptian sun god whose cult and identity were combined with other deities, including Amun.
item_facts: Ra was associated with the sun and royal authority.
He was often depicted with a falcon head and sun disk.
The name appears in compounds such as Amun-Ra and Ra-Horakhty.
needs_review: Verify forms and theological interpretations by period.

item_description: A lioness goddess associated with destructive force, healing and protection of the pharaoh.
item_facts: Sekhmet was linked with the sun god Ra.
She was often depicted as a lioness or a woman with a lioness head.
Traditions describe her power as both dangerous and protective.
needs_review: Verify myth versions and cult details using Egyptological sources.

item_description: An Egyptian deity associated with deserts, storms and disorder, but also a protector of Ra in some traditions.
item_facts: Set’s role varied across Egyptian history.
He is the rival and killer of Osiris in a well-known myth cycle.
Set assists Ra against the serpent Apophis in some accounts.
needs_review: Avoid a simple good-versus-evil portrayal; verify local and period-specific roles.

item_description: A crocodile-associated Egyptian deity linked to the Nile, fertility and royal power.
item_facts: Sobek was worshipped at sites including Kom Ombo and Crocodilopolis.
He could be depicted as a crocodile or a human with a crocodile head.
His associations included both danger and protection.
needs_review: Verify cult centers and local theological roles using Egyptological references.

item_description: A protective Egyptian goddess of childbirth, commonly depicted with features of a hippopotamus.
item_facts: Taweret was invoked for protection during pregnancy and childbirth.
Her imagery combines hippopotamus, crocodile and lion traits in some forms.
Protective figurines of Taweret were used in domestic contexts.
needs_review: Verify iconographic details and domestic practices through museum references.

item_description: An Egyptian god associated with writing, knowledge, calculation and the moon.
item_facts: Thoth was often depicted as an ibis or a baboon.
He was regarded as a scribe and record keeper among the gods.
In funerary scenes he can record the result of the heart-weighing ceremony.
needs_review: Verify textual and iconographic roles across periods.
